Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a complex problem by calling itself to break the problem down into smaller, more manageable pieces. You can think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where opening one doll reveals a slightly smaller version of itself until you finally reach the tiniest, solid doll inside. In coding, that smallest solid doll is called the "base case," which is the essential stopping condition that prevents the function from looping forever. Once the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and works its way back up the chain, combining the results of all the smaller pieces to solve the original problem.
